subject: implementer
reason: The cancel/ship 409/400/404 mapping in OrdersApi is correct, but rethrowing OrderingDomainException in the shared IdentifiedCommandHandler base changes CreateOrder and every integration-event handler: CreateOrder now escapes as an unhandled 500 and event consumers now see exceptions they never did. Root cause: a cross-cutting base class was changed for two endpoints.

items.reason: The catch/rethrow of OrderingDomainException applies to every IdentifiedCommandHandler subclass. CreateOrderAsync (OrdersApi.cs:201) has no try/catch, so a rule or validation failure on create order now becomes an unhandled exception instead of the previous handled outcome. SetPaid, SetStockConfirmed, SetStockRejected and SetAwaitingValidation event handlers now throw to the event bus on invalid transitions instead of being swallowed.
items.fix: Scope the rethrow to cancel and ship only (a virtual hook or flag on those handlers), or keep the swallow in the base class and surface rule violations another way. Keep CreateOrder and the event handlers' behaviour unchanged, or handle the exception in CreateOrderAsync explicitly.

items.reason: CreateRequestForCommandAsync persists the request id before the command runs. After a rejected cancel or ship (409/400) the id stays stored, and a retry with the same x-requestid returns 200 through the duplicate-request path, a false success for an operation that failed.
items.fix: Record the request id only after the command succeeds, or remove or roll it back when OrderingDomainException is thrown or the command returns false.

subject: implementer
reason: Rule violations map to 409/400 and a missing order to 404 in OrdersApi, using TypedResults/ProblemDetails. The opt-in ReportsFailuresToCaller flag keeps other commands' behaviour unchanged. The request id is recorded only on success inside the same transaction, so failed requests can be retried.

items.title: Cancelling a Shipped order returns 409 with the domain message, not 500
covers: Expected: 409 for cancelling a Shipped order
items.reason: This is the reported bug (steps to reproduce). Before the fix `SetCancelledStatus` threw `OrderingDomainException` and the endpoint returned 500. Functional layer because the status code is produced by `OrdersApi` plus the real command pipeline and database.

items.title: Cancelling a Paid order returns 409
items.reason: `SetCancelledStatus` rejects both Paid and Shipped; the Paid branch is a separate condition that the story's example does not exercise.

items.title: Shipping an order that is not Paid (Submitted) returns 409
items.reason: `ShipOrderAsync` had the same 500 mapping as cancel (OrdersApi.cs:74); separate endpoint, so it needs its own case.

items.title: Shipping an already Shipped order returns 409
items.reason: Covers the repeated-transition case (new request id, same target state), distinct from the not-Paid case and from duplicate request ids.

items.title: Cancelling a nonexistent order returns 404
covers: Suggested fix: return 404 when the order does not exist
items.reason: The failure path now distinguishes a missing order from a server fault. Replaces the stale expectation of 500 in `CancelNonExistentOrderFails`.

items.title: Shipping a nonexistent order returns 404
covers: Suggested fix: return 404 when the order does not exist
items.reason: Same as cancel for the ship endpoint; replaces the stale 500 expectation in `ShipNonExistentOrderFails`.

items.title: Cancel with orderNumber 0 returns 400 with the validation message
covers: Implementation Notes: validation failures map to 400
items.reason: The command validator rejects 0 (`No orderId found`); the validator failure arrives wrapped in `OrderingDomainException` and must be 400, not 409.

items.title: Ship with orderNumber 0 returns 400 with the validation message
covers: Implementation Notes: validation failures map to 400
items.reason: Mirror of the cancel validation case for the ship validator.

items.title: Cancel with an empty x-requestid still returns 400
items.reason: Regression guard: the early request-id check must still run before any rule mapping.

items.title: Ship with an empty x-requestid still returns 400
items.reason: Regression guard for the ship endpoint (`ShipWithEmptyGuidFails`).

items.title: Cancelling a Submitted order succeeds with 200
items.reason: Proves the new exception mapping does not break the success path.

items.title: Shipping a Paid order succeeds with 200
items.reason: Success path for ship after the mapping change.

items.title: Repeating a successful cancel with the same x-requestid returns 200 and changes nothing
items.reason: Idempotency path must survive the change that records request ids only on success.

items.title: Retrying a rejected cancel with the same x-requestid returns 409 again, not a false 200
covers: Implementation Notes: retry after a failed cancel/ship
items.reason: Risk: if the request id were recorded on failure, the retry would hit the duplicate path and report success for a cancel that never happened.

items.title: Retrying a cancel for a nonexistent order with the same x-requestid returns 404 both times
covers: Implementation Notes: not-found can be retried with same request id
items.reason: Same false-200 risk as TC-BUG-10-14 on the not-found path.

items.title: OrdersApi maps OrderingDomainException to 409 and a validation-wrapped one to 400
covers: Implementation Notes: 409 vs 400 mapping in OrderRuleViolation
items.reason: Cheap in-process check of both branches of the mapping using NSubstitute mocks of the mediator, in `OrdersWebApiTest`.

covers: Implementation Notes: IdentifiedCommandHandler rethrows only for opted-in handlers
items.reason: Guards the scoping so create-order and integration-event handlers keep the old default-result behavior (BUG-9 relates). In-process in `IdentifiedCommandHandlerTest`.
